name: Roflumilast cream

lead: Roflumilast (Zoryve) is a prescription cream and foam that clears the visible redness, scale and flaking of psoriasis, eczema and seborrheic dermatitis on the scalp and face. The FDA approved the 0.3% cream for plaque psoriasis in July 2022, the 0.3% foam for seborrheic dermatitis in December 2023, and a 0.15% cream for atopic dermatitis in July 2024.

It selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase-4, an enzyme involved in inflammatory signaling in skin, so inflammation and scaling settle and skin looks calmer. Phase 3 randomized trials have tested it in plaque psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. Uses such as vitiligo have no trials behind them in the sources reviewed.

paras: People apply the cream to plaques or the foam to scalp and facial areas as directed by a prescriber. It is steroid-free, used as ongoing treatment for the condition, with visible improvement building over weeks.
It is prescription only. Topical adverse events are reported in trial publications and on the label; oral roflumilast tablets list diarrhea, nausea, headache and insomnia.

angle.text: Roflumilast cream and foam clear the visible redness, scale and flaking of psoriasis, eczema and scalp or facial seborrheic dermatitis. It blocks PDE-4 to lower skin inflammation, so scalp and face look clearer. Phase 3 trials cover psoriasis and eczema.

lead: Roflumilast cream (brand name Zoryve, developed by Arcutis) is a topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor. The US FDA approved the 0.3% cream for plaque psoriasis in July 2022, a 0.3% foam for seborrheic dermatitis in December 2023, and a 0.15% cream for atopic dermatitis in July 2024.[1] Seborrheic dermatitis and psoriasis are visible skin conditions, which is the basis of its appearance relevance.
Phase 3 trials have tested it in plaque psoriasis and atopic dermatitis.[2][3] Other uses such as vitiligo are not supported by trials in the sources reviewed.

paras: Approved uses in the US are plaque psoriasis (age 12 and over), seborrheic dermatitis (foam, age 9 and over) and mild to moderate atopic dermatitis (age 6 and over for the 0.15% cream, with a 0.05% cream extended to ages 2 to 5 in October 2025).[1]
Roflumilast is a selective, long-acting PDE-4 inhibitor with anti-inflammatory effects.[1] Pharmacokinetic data from phase 1 to 3 psoriasis studies have been published.[4]

A phase 2b trial in plaque psoriasis tested 0.3% and 0.15% cream against vehicle for 12 weeks,[5] and the DERMIS-1 and DERMIS-2 phase 3 trials (about 440 participants each) tested 0.3% cream for 8 weeks.[2] A 52-week open-label study reported long-term safety and effectiveness.[6] In atopic dermatitis, phase 2 and the INTEGUMENT-1 and -2 phase 3 trials tested 0.15% cream against vehicle,[3][7] and INTEGUMENT-PED studied children aged 2 to 5.[8] Registered studies include facial papulopustular rosacea (n=40).[9] No trial for vitiligo was found, and seborrheic dermatitis trials were not among the sources reviewed.

The article on roflumilast lists oral-tablet effects such as diarrhea, nausea, headache and insomnia; topical-specific adverse events are reported in the trial publications and product label.[1][2][3]

timeline.event: FDA approves 0.3% cream for plaque psoriasis.[1]
